# structured_planning-examples dataset

Internal dataset of an AI assistant producing structured, step-by-step project plans.

- Data lives in `data/entries.dat` (one JSON object per line, fields: `prompt`, `response`).
- Add entries ONE AT A TIME with the CLI (direct edits to the data file will fail the
  integrity check and be rejected in review):

      echo '{"prompt": "...", "response": "..."}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py

- Before pushing, run `make check`.
</tool_response>

{"prompt": "I want to launch a small online store selling handmade candles within 2 months. Help me plan it out.", "response": "Here's an 8-week structure:

Weeks 1-2 (Foundation): Finalize 6-10 core products, source suppliers for wax/wicks/fragrance, settle on pricing and margins, register your business name.

Weeks 3-4 (Build): Set up your storefront (Shopify or Etsy), take product photos, write listings, set up payment and shipping.

Weeks 5-6 (Inventory + Legal): Produce initial stock (aim for 2-3x expected first-month sales), get any required candle-safety labeling sorted, set up basic bookkeeping.

Weeks 7-8 (Launch): Soft-launch to friends/email list for feedback, fix issues, then go public with a small paid ad push and social content.

Want me to break any single week into a day-by-day checklist?"}
{"prompt": "Plan out a study schedule for the MCAT over the next 4 months, I work part-time.", "response": "Given part-time work, plan roughly 15-20 hours/week across 16 weeks:

Weeks 1-6 (Content review): Work through one subject area per week (Biology, Biochem, Chem/Phys, Psych/Soc, CARS practice daily), using a content review book plus spaced-repetition flashcards.

Weeks 7-10 (Practice + gaps): Full-length practice exams every 10-12 days, spend remaining time drilling your weakest section from each exam's score breakdown.

Weeks 11-14 (Intensive practice): Increase to 2 full-lengths per week with thorough review of every wrong answer, not just right ones.

Weeks 15-16 (Taper): Light review only, no new material, protect sleep, take your last full-length at least 5 days before test day.

Want a weekly hour breakdown too?"}
{"prompt": "We need to migrate our team's project management from spreadsheets to a proper tool in the next quarter. Help me plan the rollout.", "response": "Month 1 (Evaluate + decide): Shortlist 2-3 tools based on your actual workflows, run a 1-week pilot with a small volunteer group on real work, get buy-in from team leads before committing.

Month 2 (Migrate + configure): Map your spreadsheet columns to tool fields, migrate active projects first (not historical ones), set up templates and automations, write a one-page 'how we use this' doc.

Month 3 (Adopt + reinforce): Run the tool in parallel with spreadsheets for week 1 only as a safety net, then go tool-only. Hold two short office-hours sessions for stragglers, and revisit after 6 weeks to fix friction points people actually hit.

Want a RACI chart for who owns each phase?"}
</tool_response>

<think>
I can see the format. Each entry is a JSON object with "prompt" and "response" fields. The prompts ask for project plans, and the responses give structured, step-by-step breakdowns with phases/timelines. Let me create 5 varied entries following this pattern, then add them one by one using the script.
</think>

Now I'll add 5 varied entries. Let me craft them and add each one:

<tool_call>
<function=bash>
<parameter=command>
echo '{"prompt": "I want to organize a community food drive in my neighborhood over the next 6 weeks. What should I do?", "response": "Here is a 6-week rollout plan:

Week 1 (Set the foundation): Define your goal (pounds or number of families served), pick a local food bank as your receiving partner, draft a simple timeline and budget.

Week 2 (Recruit + logistics): Recruit 4-6 volunteer organizers, secure 2-3 drop-off locations (churches, offices, cafes), create a shared spreadsheet for volunteer shifts and inventory.

Week 3 (Outreach launch): Post in neighborhood Facebook/Nextdoor groups, put up flyers at drop-off sites, contact 5-10 local businesses for in-kind donations (boxes, bags, gas cards).

Week 4 (Collection mode): Open all drop-off sites, run a 48-hour "double your impact" challenge if the food bank can match donations, post daily update photos to keep momentum.

Week 5 (Wrap collection + sort): Close drop-off sites by Wednesday, schedule a Saturday sorting event (by-expiry-date bins, team leads per table), confirm pickup date/time with food bank.

Week 6 (Deliver + reflect): Load and deliver sorted donations, send a thank-you blast with final numbers to all volunteers and donors, hold a 20-minute debrief call to document lessons learned.

Want me to draft the volunteer recruitment email?"}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

<think>
Entry 1 added. Now entry 2 - let me do a software release planning one.
</think>

<tool_call>
<function=bash>
<parameter=command>
echo '{"prompt": "Help me plan a 10-week sprint to build and launch an MVP for a task-management app for remote teams.", "response": "Here is a 10-week MVP sprint plan:

Weeks 1-2 (Discovery + scope): Interview 8-10 target users to validate the core pain point, finalize a one-screen feature list (create tasks, assign, status tracking, Slack notifications), sketch low-fidelity wireframes.

Weeks 3-4 (Core build): Set up the tech stack (React frontend, Node/Postgres backend), implement user auth and the task CRUD flow, get a clickable prototype running on localhost.

Weeks 5-6 (Collaboration layer): Add team workspaces, task assignments, and notification system, integrate Slack Webhooks for real-time updates, write automated tests for critical paths.

Weeks 7-8 (Polish + deploy): Deploy to a staging environment (Vercel + Render), fix UI quirks and edge cases, set up basic analytics and error monitoring.

Weeks 9-10 (Beta launch): Invite 15-20 teams to a closed beta, collect daily feedback in a dedicated channel, prioritize and ship top-5 fixes before a public landing-page launch.

Want a detailed feature-backlog template?"}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

<think>
Entry 2 added. Now entry 3 - something about planning a road trip.
</think>

<tool_call>
<function=bash>
<parameter=command>
echo '{"prompt": "I need a plan to save $15,000 for a down payment on a car within 15 months. I currently have $3,000 saved.", "response": "You need $12,000 more, which is $800/month for 15 months. Here is how to structure it:

Month 1 (Diagnose): Print last 3 months of bank/credit-card statements, categorize every dollar (50/30/20 framework), identify the 3 biggest flexible spending categories.

Months 2-4 (Automate the core): Set up a $500/month automatic transfer to a separate high-yield savings account on payday, negotiate or switch at least one recurring bill (phone, internet, insurance) for $150-200/month savings.

Months 5-8 (Fill the gap): Find $300/month through side income (freelance gig, weekend shifts, selling unused items online) or by cutting discretionary spending (subscriptions, dining out, impulse shopping).

Months 9-12 (Protect the runway): Build a $1,000 mini-emergency buffer in the same account so you never have to dip into the fund, review progress at the start of every month and adjust if you are off track by more than 10%.

Months 13-15 (Finish strong): If you are behind, add one big action (sell a large item, take a one-time contract) to close the gap, lock in the savings goal date and treat it like a non-negotiable bill.

Want a printable monthly tracker template?"}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

<think>
Entry 3 added. Now entry 4 - let me do something about launching a newsletter.
</think>

<tool_call>
<function=bash>
<parameter=command>
echo '{"prompt": "Plan a 12-week strategy to grow a new personal newsletter from 0 to 1,000 subscribers.", "response": "Here is a 12-week growth plan:

Weeks 1-2 (Positioning): Pick a tight niche (e.g., "AI tools for non-technical founders" not just "tech"), write a one-sentence value prop, design a clean landing page with a clear sign-up incentive (free cheat sheet or template).

Weeks 3-4 (Content engine): Batch-write 4 issue drafts, set a cadence (e.g., every other Tuesday), add a referral program ("share to unlock a bonus episode"), install a tracking pixel to measure which channels convert best.

Weeks 5-8 (Outbound push): Post 3x/week on Twitter/LinkedIn with snippets + link, comment thoughtfully on 10 industry threads daily, pitch 2 guest appearances on small podcasts, collaborate on 1 cross-promotion with a similar-sized newsletter.

Weeks 9-10 (Amplification): Launch a LinkedIn carousel summarizing your best newsletter insight with a CTA, run a 7-day "best-ever issue" promotion, ask your first 50 readers for testimonials to use as social proof.

Weeks 11-12 (Analyze + double down): Identify your top-2 acquisition channels, reallocate time from zero-ROI activities, set up an automated welcome sequence that introduces you and sets expectations, plan content calendar for next quarter.

Want a swipe file of subject lines that hit 50%+ open rates?"}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

<think>
Entry 4 added. Now entry 5 - let me do something about home renovation/renovating a kitchen.
</think>

<tool_call>
<function=bash>
<parameter=command>
echo '{"prompt": "Help me plan a kitchen remodel on a budget of $20,000, finishing in about 3 months.", "response": "Here is a 12-week remodel plan:

Weeks 1-2 (Scope + budget): Walk the room with a tape measure, sketch the layout, assign budget buckets (40% cabinets/counters, 20% appliances, 15% flooring, 15% labor/misc, 10% contingency). Decide which tasks you can DIY to save costs.

Weeks 3-4 (Design + permits): Finalize material selections (sample counters in-store, compare cabinet suppliers online vs local), get 3 contractor quotes for any work needing licensed pros, pull required permits from your city.

Weeks 5-6 (Demo + rough-ins): Clear the kitchen, demo old cabinets/fixtures (bag debris, check for asbestos if pre-1980), any electrical/plumbing rough-in work, order long-lead items (custom cabinets, appliance delivery).

Weeks 7-8 (Install base): Lay flooring first, install cabinets and counters, connect plumbing lines to sink and dishwasher, test for level and square before caulking.

Weeks 9-10 (Finishes): Paint walls/trim, install backsplash, hang light fixtures and outlets, mount shelves and hardware, deep-clean all surfaces.

Weeks 11-12 (Appliances + punch list): Bring in and connect appliances, run the sink/dishtwasher/garbage disposal for leaks, walk the room with your punch-list clipboard, fix final gaps/scares, stage with nice dishes and call it done.

Want a shared spreadsheet template for tracking quotes and purchases?"}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
